Algebra.title: Algebra
Algebra.description: Algebra studies structures defined by operations and the laws, morphisms, and symmetries that organize them.

fields.title: Rings and fields
fields.description: Elementary theory of semirings, rings, division rings and fields: homomorphisms and isomorphisms, subrings and subfields, units, idempotents, characteristic and Frobenius, Boolean rings, formally real rings and sums of squares. Divisibility has its own field, ideals and local rings are under ring theory, and extensions of fields are under field theory.

fields.title: Divisibility and greatest common divisors
fields.description: Divisibility in monoids and rings: units and associated elements, irreducible, prime and primal elements, cancellative and regular elements, normalization and GCD monoids, greatest common divisors and least common multiples of finite families; unique factorization domains and ideal-theoretic factorization are under Ring Theory, divisibility of integers under Number Theory.

fields.title: Ordered algebraic structures
fields.description: Monoids, groups, rings, fields and modules with compatible orders: monotone operations, positive cones, lattice-ordered groups and their order-induced absolute values, ring orderings, Archimedean properties, floor and ceiling functions, and order-preserving maps. Orders and lattices as such are under order theory, orderable groups under group theory, and general absolute values and their completions under analysis.

subfields.title: Ordered monoids and groups
subfields.description: Ordered, canonically ordered and linearly ordered monoids and groups: monotonicity of multiplication, truncated subtraction, absolute values, positive and negative parts, lattice-ordered groups, adjoined top and bottom elements, ordered groups with zero, order-preserving monoid homomorphisms and arithmetic of intervals.

subfields.title: Ordered rings and fields
subfields.description: Ordered semirings, rings and fields: positivity and monotonicity of multiplication, order-induced absolute values, positive and nonnegative elements as algebraic structures, positive cones and ring orderings, ordered modules and algebras, and star-ordered rings.

subfields.title: Archimedean structures and floor functions
subfields.description: Archimedean ordered groups and fields, Archimedean classes and the Hahn embedding theorem, conditionally complete ordered fields, floor and ceiling functions, fractional part and rounding, and reduction modulo an interval.

fields.title: Finite sums and products
fields.description: Sums and products over finite sets, multisets, lists and finitely supported families in commutative monoids: reindexing, splitting and interchange of sums, sums over intervals and antidiagonals, averages, sums in rings and groups with zero, inequalities for finite sums in ordered structures and congruences of sums; infinite sums are under Topology.

fields.title: Star rings and involutions
fields.description: Involutions on monoids, rings and algebras; self-adjoint, skew-adjoint, normal and unitary elements, projections, star homomorphisms and star subalgebras. Star-ordered rings are under ordered algebraic structures, and C⋆-algebras under analysis.

fields.title: Modules over rings
fields.description: Modules over rings and semirings: linear maps and equivalences, submodules and their lattice, kernels and images, torsion and torsion-free modules, projective, injective and finitely presented modules, presentations, localization of modules, direct limits and ℤ-lattices. Vector spaces, bases, dimension and matrices are under linear algebra; module-theoretic results of commutative algebra are under ring theory.

fields.title: Associative rings and algebras
fields.description: Noncommutative rings and finite-dimensional associative algebras, including division and central simple algebras, quaternion algebras, polynomial identities, nil ideals and Hopf algebras. Group rings are under Group Theory.

fields.title: Direct sums and graded structures
fields.description: Direct sums of groups and modules, internal direct sum decompositions, and graded monoids, rings, algebras and modules, including gradings of monoid algebras. Homogeneous ideals and projective spectra are under ring theory; tensor products are under linear algebra.

fields.title: Lie algebras and nonassociative structures
fields.description: Lie algebras and their structure and representations, free Lie algebras, Poisson algebras, and racks and quandles.

fields.title: Algebraic identities and operations
fields.description: Polynomial and product identities, sum-of-squares identities, functional equations on rings, and elementary operations on functions and sets.

fields.title: Polynomials and power series
fields.description: Univariate and multivariate polynomials and formal power series as algebraic objects: coefficients, derivations, symmetric polynomials, irreducibility, polynomial maps and rational series.

subfields.title: Univariate polynomial arithmetic
subfields.description: Arithmetic of polynomials in one indeterminate: coefficients and monomials, degree and leading terms, evaluation and composition, formal differentiation and Taylor expansion, and division with remainder. Multivariate polynomials, special irreducibility criteria and formal power series remain in the parent field; zeros and their multiplicities have their own field.

fields.title: Zeros of polynomials
fields.description: Location, counting and multiplicity of the zeros of polynomials: real-rootedness, stability, interlacing, root bounds and Sturm sequences.

fields.title: Orthogonal polynomials and polynomial sequences
fields.description: Classical and combinatorial families of polynomials, their recurrences and generating functions, and orthogonality via Favard's theorem, J-fractions and Riordan arrays.

fields.title: Categories of algebraic structures
fields.description: Concrete categories of algebraic objects (semigroups, monoids, groups, rings, algebras, coalgebras, Hopf algebras and modules), their limits, colimits, adjunctions and monoidal structures, and presheaves and sheaves of modules. General category theory and abelian categories as such are under category theory.

subfields.title: Categories of groups and monoids
subfields.description: Categories of semigroups, monoids, groups, groups with zero and abelian groups: limits and colimits, free–forgetful adjunctions, monomorphisms and epimorphisms, and the abelian category of abelian groups.

subfields.title: Categories of rings and algebras
subfields.description: Categories of rings, commutative rings, Boolean rings, algebras, coalgebras, bialgebras and Hopf algebras over a commutative ring: limits, colimits, adjunctions and monoidal structures.

subfields.title: Categories of modules
subfields.description: Categories of modules and finitely generated modules over a ring: abelian and monoidal structure, change of rings, injective and projective objects, Ext over a ring, and topological modules. Presheaves and sheaves of modules have their own subfield.

subfields.title: Presheaves and sheaves of modules
subfields.description: Presheaves and sheaves of modules over presheaves and sheaves of rings on a site: limits and colimits, sheafification, pullback and pushforward, internal Hom, free, locally free and quasi-coherent sheaves of modules, presheaves of differentials, and the cohomology of ringed sites with its cup product.

AlgebraicGeometry.title: Algebraic Geometry
AlgebraicGeometry.description: Algebraic geometry studies spaces cut out by polynomial equations and translates between their geometric and algebraic invariants.

fields.title: Schemes and morphisms
fields.description: The scheme-theoretic foundations of algebraic geometry: points, immersions, smooth morphisms, varieties over a field, consequences of Zariski's main theorem, properties that persist under base change, projective space over a ring, the Segre embedding and Chow's lemma, algebraic cycles and Weil divisors, the correspondence between affine group schemes and commutative Hopf algebras, the smoothness of geometrically reduced group schemes over a field, effective epimorphisms and the cotangent complex of a morphism of schemes, with subfields for sheaves of modules on schemes, derived categories of coherent sheaves, determinants of perfect complexes and Deligne pairings, and Frobenius and perfection in characteristic p.

subfields.title: Derived categories of coherent sheaves
subfields.description: Derived categories of quasi-coherent and coherent sheaves on schemes: derived pullback (on affine schemes too), pushforward and tensor product, Fourier–Mukai transforms and their composition, spherical twists, exceptional collections, stability conditions, Grothendieck duality with its base change, and the formality of derived self-intersections. Determinants of perfect complexes have their own subfield, and dg enhancements and moduli of objects are under derived algebraic geometry.

subfields.title: Determinants of perfect complexes and Deligne pairings
subfields.description: Knudsen–Mumford determinants of perfect complexes on schemes: determinants of two-term and bounded perfect complexes, their compatibility with extension of scalars and derived pullback, global determinant lines glued from affine presentations, torsion of acyclic complexes, and Deligne pairings of line bundles on relative schemes with their symbols, norms and cubical structures. Determinants of the cohomology of families of curves are under algebraic curves.

subfields.title: Frobenius and perfection in characteristic p
subfields.description: Schemes in characteristic p: the absolute and geometric Frobenius morphisms and their naturality, perfect schemes, and the perfection of a scheme, the limit along Frobenius (the colimit of its rings of functions), with its universal property for maps from perfect schemes. F-singularities are under birational geometry, arc descent under Grothendieck topologies, and perfectoid spaces under nonarchimedean geometry.

subfields.title: Sheaves of modules on schemes
subfields.description: Sheaves of modules on schemes: sheafified tensor products, exterior powers and the projection formula, global sections and base change, line bundles with their tensor powers, pullbacks, duals and algebraic families, rational functions and divisorial sheaves, total spaces and projective bundles of locally free sheaves, traces of endomorphisms, and sheaves of Kähler differentials and differential forms. The category of sheaves of modules on a scheme, quasi-coherent sheaves on affine schemes, and presheaves and sheaves of modules on general sites are under categories of algebraic structures, and the cotangent complex of a ring map under ring theory.

fields.title: Grothendieck topologies and étale cohomology
fields.description: Sites attached to schemes: the Zariski, étale, pro-étale, fppf, fpqc, arc and quasi-compact topologies, their points, sheaves and torsors, Čech complexes of covers and descent along these covers, arc descent included, representability of sheaves by schemes, and the definition of ℓ-adic cohomology as pro-étale cohomology with ℓ-adic coefficients, with subfields for étale cohomology, for pro-étale and ℓ-adic cohomology, and for nearby and vanishing cycles. Grothendieck topologies and sheaves on general sites are under category theory.

subfields.title: Étale cohomology
subfields.description: Cohomology of sheaves on the small étale site with torsion coefficients: the Kummer sequence, Tate twists and Kummer classes, derived global sections, restriction, corestriction and traces along finite flat morphisms, localization and residues at discrete valuations, derived categories of étale sheaves of modules with their constructible complexes and dg enhancements, and Gabber's prime-to-ℓ alterations. Sites, topologies and descent, arc descent included, and the definition of ℓ-adic cohomology stay in the parent field; the rest of the theory with continuous and ℓ-adic coefficients is in pro-étale and ℓ-adic cohomology, and nearby cycles in nearby and vanishing cycles.

subfields.title: Pro-étale and ℓ-adic cohomology
subfields.description: Cohomology of schemes on the pro-étale site with continuous coefficients, after Bhatt and Scholze: sheaves of modules on the pro-étale site and their derived functors, compactly supported cohomology through compactifications, the actions of Galois groups and of Frobenius on ℓ-adic cohomology, Frobenius elements in étale fundamental groups and lisse ℓ-adic sheaves with Lafforgue's purity theorem, and Katz's bound for sums of Betti numbers. The pro-étale site and the definition of cohomology with ℓ-adic coefficients stay in the parent field.

subfields.title: Nearby and vanishing cycles
subfields.description: Nearby and vanishing cycles of étale and ℓ-adic sheaves on schemes: strict localizations and Milnor fibres, local acyclicity, Beilinson's singular support, Saito's characteristic cycle with the total dimension and Swan conductors of vanishing cycles over curves, and semistable degenerations over a henselian trait with the inertia action on nearby cycles, the local monodromy theorem for them and the Weil–Deligne representations on their cohomology. Nearby cycles of complex varieties are under constructible sheaves and D-modules, p-adic nearby cycles under p-adic cohomology, and Weil–Deligne representations and Grothendieck's ℓ-adic monodromy theorem for Galois representations as such under Galois representations and p-adic Hodge theory.

fields.title: Varieties and projective geometry
fields.description: Classical algebraic geometry of affine and projective varieties: hypersurfaces and their singularities, tangent spaces, plane configurations, intersection multiplicities, flag and Schubert varieties, weighted projective spaces, Hilbert schemes of points on surfaces, jet schemes and arc spaces, multivariate resultants, counts of solutions of sparse polynomial systems, tropical varieties, linear systems and birational maps, with subfields for toric and tropical geometry and for real algebraic geometry.

subfields.title: Toric and tropical geometry
subfields.description: Toric varieties of fans and their homogeneous coordinate rings, Cox's quotient construction, Minkowski weights and operational Chow rings of toric varieties, tropicalizations and balanced polyhedral complexes, tropical intersection multiplicities and the lifting of tropical intersections, and degrees of tropicalizations on skeletons. Tropical varieties of polynomial systems as such are in the parent field.

subfields.title: Real algebraic geometry
subfields.description: Real algebraic and semialgebraic geometry: semialgebraic sets and maps over ordered rings and real closed fields, closure under projection (Tarski–Seidenberg), Hardt's semialgebraic triviality, real algebraic varieties with their nonsingular stratifications, and real algebraic and stratified-algebraic vector bundles. Quantifier elimination for real closed fields is under model theory.

fields.title: Birational geometry and vanishing theorems
fields.description: Resolution of singularities and principalization of ideals in characteristic zero, and explicit resolutions such as that of the crossing xy = t^e over any commutative ring, vanishing theorems (Kodaira, Kawamata–Viehweg, Nadel), multiplier ideals, positivity of line bundles and divisors (nef and big classes, volumes), L² extension theorems with currents of integration and the Poincaré–Lelong formula, and, in subfields, singularities of pairs with the minimal model program and K-stability of Fano varieties. Rational maps of particular varieties, Cremona groups, linear systems on projective space and intersection multiplicities are under varieties and projective geometry, and complex manifolds as such under complex and symplectic geometry.

subfields.title: K-stability of Fano varieties
subfields.description: K-stability of Fano varieties and polarized varieties: test configurations and their Duistermaat–Heckman measures, nonarchimedean functionals, log discrepancies and expected vanishing orders of valuations, Fujita's valuative criterion and the beta invariant, openness of K-semistability in families, and uniqueness of K-polystable degenerations.

subfields.title: Singularities of pairs and the minimal model program
subfields.description: Discrepancies and klt, log canonical, dlt and plt pairs, adjunction and the different, multiplier ideals on normal varieties and log canonical thresholds, rational and Du Bois singularities, Nash blowups, Grauert–Riemenschneider vanishing, conductors and gluing involutions of demi-normal schemes, the characteristic-p theory of Frobenius trace maps, test ideals and F-adjunction, and the minimal model program: the Mori cone, the cone, contraction and flip theorems in absolute and relative form, dlt models, pl-flips and restricted algebras, deformation invariance of plurigenera, and reflexive powers of relative canonical sheaves with Kollár's condition in families.

fields.title: Algebraic curves
fields.description: Algebraic curves and their invariants, including divisors, the genus, coherent cohomology and linear series, Jacobians and the Abel–Jacobi map, determinants of cohomology in families, fine compactified Jacobians of reduced curves, moduli of stable marked curves, and theta functions on the Drinfeld upper half plane.

fields.title: Elliptic curves
fields.description: Elliptic curves given by Weierstrass equations, their points over finite fields and number fields, torsion, reduction and Galois representations.

fields.title: Abelian varieties and abelian schemes
fields.description: Abelian varieties over fields: duals and polarizations, Zarhin's trick, the Néron model of an abelian variety and semistable reduction, complex multiplication, fake elliptic curves with their canonical polarizations and special formal O_D-modules, the p-divisible groups of abelian schemes and their deformations (Serre–Tate, Grothendieck–Messing), and moduli of polarized abelian varieties, including toroidal and minimal compactifications in the principally polarized case, and degenerations through semi-abelian schemes, with a subfield for abelian schemes over a general base. Jacobians of curves are under algebraic curves, and abelian varieties of dimension one under elliptic curves.

subfields.title: Abelian schemes
subfields.description: Abelian schemes over a general base: their duals, homomorphisms and isogenies, Zarhin's trick for abelian schemes, semi-abelian schemes and their Lie algebras, and Néron models over a discrete valuation ring defined by their mapping property, with the reduction of points; also the torsion and Verschiebung of abelian varieties in characteristic p, and the first ℓ-adic cohomology of an abelian variety as the dual of its Tate module.

fields.title: Arithmetic geometry
fields.description: Rational points, zero-cycles and point counts of varieties over number fields and finite fields, including the Mordell conjecture, the Weil conjectures, the Brauer–Manin pairing on zero-cycles and unramified cohomology. The Hasse principle and its failures for rational points are under number theory's arithmetic geometry.

fields.title: Arakelov geometry
fields.description: Arithmetic varieties over the integers or over rings of integers, with hermitian vector bundles and Green currents on their complex points: arithmetic Chow groups and intersection theory, arithmetic Chern classes and degrees, the arithmetic Riemann–Roch and Hilbert–Samuel theorems, arithmetic volumes and positivity of hermitian line bundles, and Arakelov divisors of number fields, with a subfield for adelic metrics and heights. Heights of algebraic numbers and of points of projective space are under heights and Mahler measure.

subfields.title: Adelic metrics and heights
subfields.description: Line bundles with metrics at all places of a field: metrics on fibres over Berkovich and archimedean points, model metrics from integral and arithmetic models, hermitian model metrics and their local Chern currents, completion of model metrics on quasi-projective varieties, nef and integrable adelic metrics and their Picard group, and the heights they define: heights of points, zero-cycles and cycles, heights of Chow forms included, and Néron–Tate heights on abelian varieties. Heights of algebraic numbers and of points of projective space as such are under heights and Mahler measure.

fields.title: Group schemes
fields.description: Group schemes over general bases and their actions: finite locally free group schemes with Cartier duality and invariant differentials, p-divisible groups over a general base with their Cartier duals, Lie algebras, Tate modules and Hodge–Tate maps, general linear groups, tori and reductive group schemes, degrees of endomorphisms, torsors and associated bundles, linearized line bundles and geometric invariant theory, and quotients by finite groups. The correspondence between affine group schemes and commutative Hopf algebras, and the smoothness of geometrically reduced group schemes over a field, are under schemes and morphisms; torsors as sheaves on a site under Grothendieck topologies; crystalline Dieudonné theory under p-adic cohomology; the Hodge–Tate sequence of p-divisible groups over O_C under Galois representations and p-adic Hodge theory; and abelian varieties and abelian schemes, with the finite locally free group schemes and p-divisible groups from which their deformation theory starts and the deformations themselves (Serre–Tate, Grothendieck–Messing), under abelian varieties.

fields.title: Algebraic spaces and stacks
fields.description: Algebraic spaces and algebraic stacks over schemes: fppf stacks in groupoids, representable morphisms, smooth and étale atlases, Artin and Deligne–Mumford stacks, small fppf sites, quasi-coherent sheaves and vector bundles on stacks, Chow groups of Artin stacks, vector bundle stacks and intrinsic normal cones, Θ-reductivity and S-completeness, moduli stacks of complexes, and motivic Hall algebras with their integration maps. Descent data and stacks over general sites are under category theory.

fields.title: Logarithmic geometry
fields.description: Log structures on ringed sites and schemes: characteristic monoids and charts, fine and saturated log schemes, log smooth morphisms, log curves and basic stable log maps, Deligne–Faltings structures, root stacks and infinite root stacks, the Kummer-flat topology, and parabolic sheaves. Log pairs and discrepancies of the minimal model program are under birational geometry.

fields.title: Derived algebraic geometry
fields.description: Algebraic geometry over simplicial commutative rings: derived prestacks and stacks for the étale topology, derived Artin stacks, quasi-coherent sheaves and cotangent complexes of derived stacks, differential forms and closed forms, shifted symplectic and Lagrangian structures, moduli of objects in dg categories, Calabi–Yau structures on dg categories with the Hochschild and cyclic homology of dg algebras they rest on, and dg enhancements of quasi-coherent sheaves and perfect complexes on schemes. Derived categories of quasi-coherent and coherent sheaves on schemes are under schemes and morphisms, and dg categories and dg modules as such under homological algebra.

subfields.title: Cotangent complexes and derived deformation theory
subfields.description: Square-zero extensions and spaces of derivations of derived prestacks, cotangent complexes at points and as global quasi-coherent modules corepresenting derivations, and the cotangent differentials of morphisms. The cotangent complex of a ring map is under ring theory, that of a morphism of schemes under schemes and morphisms, and perfect obstruction theories under enumerative geometry.

subfields.title: Derived stacks
subfields.description: Simplicial commutative algebras and derived affine schemes, derived prestacks with their mapping prestacks and categories of affine points, derived stacks for the étale topology and their homotopy fibre products, and derived Artin stacks with smooth atlases and open substacks. Algebraic spaces and stacks over classical schemes are under algebraic spaces and stacks.

subfields.title: Differential forms on derived stacks
subfields.description: Graded mixed de Rham complexes of simplicial commutative algebras and weighted negative cyclic complexes, spaces of p-forms and closed p-forms of degree n on derived prestacks, and the identification of forms on derived Artin stacks with sections of exterior powers of the cotangent complex. Algebraic de Rham cohomology of schemes in characteristic zero is under Hodge theory, and the de Rham complex in characteristic p under p-adic cohomology.

subfields.title: Moduli of objects in dg categories
subfields.description: The derived moduli stack of objects of a dg category of finite type (Toën–Vaquié), its points and tangent complexes, and its comparison with classical stacks of perfect complexes on the locus of objects without negative self-extensions. Modules over dg categories and derived Morita theory are under homological algebra, and classical stacks of complexes on algebraic spaces under algebraic spaces and stacks.

subfields.title: Quasi-coherent sheaves on derived stacks
subfields.description: Quasi-coherent and perfect modules on derived prestacks as cocartesian sections over their affine points, their stable dg enhancements, tensor products, duals and cup products, and derived global sections computed by descent over affine points. Derived categories of quasi-coherent and coherent sheaves on classical schemes are under schemes and morphisms, and modules over dg categories as such under homological algebra.

subfields.title: Shifted symplectic and Lagrangian structures
subfields.description: Shifted symplectic forms and their nondegeneracy, isotropic and Lagrangian structures on morphisms, shifted symplectic structures on derived Lagrangian intersections, O-compact derived stacks with orientations, integration of forms along them and the transgression of shifted symplectic structures to derived mapping stacks. d-critical loci are under enumerative geometry, and symplectic manifolds under complex and symplectic geometry.

fields.title: Intersection theory
fields.description: Algebraic cycles and their intersections on schemes: Chow groups with flat pullback and proper pushforward, Chern and Segre classes and operational Chow groups, normal cones, refined Gysin maps and the excess intersection formula, intersection numbers of line bundles, algebraic K-theory of perfect complexes and coherent sheaves, and equivariant intersection theory of torus actions: equivariant Chow groups, localization to fixed loci, Borel equivariant cohomology and stable envelopes. Algebraic cycles and Weil divisors as such are under schemes and morphisms, intersection multiplicities of plane curves and hypersurfaces under varieties and projective geometry, Chow groups of stacks under algebraic spaces and stacks, and virtual classes under enumerative geometry.

fields.title: Enumerative geometry and virtual classes
fields.description: Virtual fundamental classes of moduli spaces with perfect obstruction theories and their cosection and torus localization, moduli of stable maps and quasimaps, relative stable maps, expanded degenerations and the degeneration formula, rubber maps and double ramification cycles, and stable pairs and Donaldson–Thomas theory with d-critical loci and the Behrend function.

subfields.title: Donaldson–Thomas theory
subfields.description: Stable pairs on threefolds and their fine moduli, truncated Atiyah classes and the perfect obstruction theory of stable pairs, d-critical loci with their canonical bundles and orientations, and the Behrend function of schemes and stacks.

subfields.title: Relative stable maps and the degeneration formula
subfields.description: Jun Li's expanded degenerations and expanded relative pairs, relative and predeformable stable maps with contact orders along a divisor, their deformation complexes, perfect obstruction theories and virtual classes, the degeneration formula, rubber maps and double ramification cycles, and Pixton's formula for them.

subfields.title: Stable maps and quasimaps
subfields.description: Families and moduli of stable maps from marked nodal curves and their curve classes, deformation and obstruction theory of maps and of evaluation maps, composition with maps of targets and stabilization, the branch morphism of maps to curves, and quasimaps to GIT quotients with their base points, degrees and regularization.

subfields.title: Perfect obstruction theories and virtual classes
subfields.description: Perfect obstruction theories and their comparison with the cotangent complex, virtual fundamental classes and virtual pullbacks, localization of virtual classes by cosections, and the virtual localization formula for torus actions. Vector bundle stacks and intrinsic normal cones are under algebraic spaces and stacks.

fields.title: Moduli of bundles and geometric Langlands
fields.description: Vector bundles and principal bundles on curves and their moduli, as used in the geometric Langlands program: slope stability, Harder–Narasimhan filtrations, moduli of stable bundles and universal families; Higgs bundles, Hitchin fibrations, spectral and cameral covers; loop groups and affine Grassmannians over power series and over Witt vectors; G-torsors on discs and their Hecke modifications; and shtukas. Jacobians and compactified Jacobians are under algebraic curves.

subfields.title: Affine Grassmannians and loop groups
subfields.description: Loop groups and positive loop groups of reductive groups over Laurent series and over Witt vectors of perfect rings, unramified or ramified, and the affine Grassmannian: as the fpqc quotient of the loop group, as the moduli of G-torsors on a disc trivialized on the punctured disc and, for the general linear group, through lattices; its representability by ind-schemes and by ind-perfect projective schemes; the loop group action and the convolution product.

subfields.title: Higgs bundles and Hitchin fibrations
subfields.description: Higgs bundles on curves and on higher-dimensional varieties and their stability, the Hitchin base and Hitchin map, spectral curves and the Beauville–Narasimhan–Ramanan correspondence, cameral covers and the abelianization of G-Higgs bundles, and the topology of Hitchin fibrations, including the perverse filtration and P = W. The correspondence with flat bundles through harmonic metrics is under Hodge theory.

fields.title: Hodge theory and transcendental methods
fields.description: Transcendental methods for complex algebraic varieties: the complex analytic space of a scheme, GAGA and coherent analytic cohomology, algebraic and holomorphic de Rham cohomology, Hodge structures on the cohomology of smooth proper varieties, limits of variations of Hodge structure and Hodge modules on curves, lattices and periods of K3 surfaces and hyperkähler manifolds, flat bundles and their monodromy, and nonabelian Hodge theory. Complex manifolds as such are under complex and symplectic geometry.

fields.title: Constructible sheaves and D-modules
fields.description: Sheaves and D-modules on complex algebraic varieties and complex manifolds: cycle classes, Gysin maps and Chern classes in Betti cohomology, constructible functions and Euler characteristics, constructible complexes and perverse sheaves, intersection complexes and the decomposition theorem, nearby and vanishing cycles, analytic and right D-modules with good and V-filtrations, holonomic and regular singular D-modules, ind-sheaves of D-modules, subanalytic sheaves and tempered holomorphic functions, and the regular and irregular Riemann–Hilbert correspondences. Sheaves and ind-sheaves on topological spaces as such are under sheaves on topological spaces.

fields.title: Motivic homotopy theory
fields.description: The homotopy theory of smooth schemes in which the affine line is contractible, and motivic cohomology: the Nisnevich topology, finite correspondences and Nisnevich sheaves with transfers, motivic complexes and their products, pointed motivic spaces and the motivic homotopy category, motivic Eilenberg–MacLane spaces, Thom and Euler classes of vector bundles, geometric classifying spaces of finite groups, the total power construction for finite relative cycles, and Bockstein and reduced power operations.

fields.title: p-adic cohomology
fields.description: Cohomology of schemes and p-adic formal schemes in characteristic p and mixed characteristic: crystalline sites, crystals and the crystalline Dieudonné theory of p-divisible groups; the de Rham complex in characteristic p and the Deligne–Illusie decomposition; prismatic cohomology over a prism and absolute prismatic cohomology, with base change, Breuil–Kisin twists, the Nygaard filtration and the crystalline and de Rham comparisons; syntomic cohomology and p-adic nearby cycles; the Hodge–Tate comparison for proper smooth varieties over p-adic fields; and the relative de Rham comparison for proper smooth rigid-analytic varieties. Period rings, p-adic Galois representations, and the prismatic background of the classification of crystalline lattices are under Galois representations and p-adic Hodge theory.

fields.title: Nonarchimedean analytic geometry
fields.description: Analytic geometry over complete nonarchimedean fields: affinoid algebras, Berkovich spectra and the Berkovich analytification of schemes, formal schemes and their generic fibres, skeletons of semistable models, Huber's adic spectra and analytic adic spaces with the pro-étale site of an analytic adic space, perfectoid spaces and diamonds, and Fargues–Fontaine curves. p-adic comparison theorems for the cohomology of varieties are under p-adic cohomology.

subfields.title: Fargues–Fontaine curves
subfields.description: The Fargues–Fontaine curve of a perfectoid space for a nonarchimedean local field of mixed or equal characteristic: the punctured period annulus and its Frobenius quotient, structure sheaf and vector bundles, functoriality and families over perfectoid bases, untilts as degree-one Cartier divisors with their B⁺_dR completions, and G-torsors and the prestack of G-bundles on the curve.

subfields.title: Perfectoid spaces and diamonds
subfields.description: Perfectoid Tate rings and affinoid perfectoid spaces, tilting and the tilting equivalence for étale and pro-étale sites, the v-topology and v-sheaves, diamonds and the diamond of an analytic adic space, small v-stacks and v-hypercovers, and the mod p Riemann–Hilbert correspondence for étale sheaves on perfectoid spaces. Solid quasi-coherent sheaves on perfectoid spaces are under condensed mathematics.

Analysis.title: Analysis
Analysis.description: Analysis studies limits, approximation, continuity, and infinite-dimensional spaces of functions and operators.

fields.title: Real functions and calculus
fields.description: Functions of one or several real variables: differentiation, partial derivatives and multivariable calculus, the Riemann integral and evaluation of definite integrals, continuity and pathological functions, and functional equations on the reals.

subfields.title: Differential calculus of one variable
subfields.description: Derivatives of real functions of one real variable: mean-value and second-derivative tests, Taylor polynomials and remainders, Borel's lemma, interchange of limits and derivatives, monotone and C^n gluing results; not nowhere-differentiable constructions (see continuity subfield).

subfields.title: Multivariable calculus
subfields.description: Functions on R^n: partial derivatives, gradients, Jacobians, Hessians, implicit functions, regular level sets and tangent spaces, curve length, Green's theorem, multivariable Taylor expansions and counterexamples about mixed partials or continuity at the origin.

subfields.title: Riemann integration and definite integrals
subfields.description: The Riemann integral via tagged partitions, iterated-integral formulas, moments, and closed-form evaluations of specific definite integrals (Serret's integral, integrals of 1/(1+u^n), areas between cosine powers, sinc squared); integrals defining a named special function go to Special functions.

subfields.title: Continuity, regularity and functional equations
subfields.description: Fine structure of real functions: Blumberg's theorem, continuous nowhere-differentiable functions (Weierstrass, Takagi), the rising sun lemma, approximate continuity, midpoint convexity, and the Cauchy, exponential and almost-additive functional equations including Hyers–Ulam stability.

fields.title: Differential calculus in normed spaces
fields.description: Differentiation on normed spaces, from Fréchet derivatives and tangent cones to smooth and analytic maps, inverse functions, vector fields and differential forms. Gradients, the implicit function theorem, symmetry of mixed partials and multivariable Taylor formulas remain under Real functions and calculus, including their normed-space formulations.

subfields.title: Fréchet derivatives
subfields.description: The Fréchet derivative and the derivative of functions of one variable over a normed field: rules for sums, products, compositions, inverses and linear and bilinear maps, strict differentiability, mean value inequalities, tangent cones and unique differentiability, and line (Gateaux) derivatives.

subfields.title: Higher derivatives and smooth maps
subfields.description: Iterated Fréchet and ordinary derivatives, finite-order Taylor jets, Cⁿ maps, bounds on higher derivatives, the Faà di Bruno formula, smooth bump functions and termwise differentiation. Convergent power series belong to Analytic maps and power series, and symmetry of mixed partials to Multivariable calculus.

subfields.title: Analytic maps and power series
subfields.description: Formal multilinear series and their radius of convergence, analytic maps between normed spaces, change of origin, composition and inversion of power series, continuously polynomial maps, the binomial series, and the principle of isolated zeros and uniqueness of analytic continuation.

fields.title: Inequalities
fields.description: Classical inequalities for sums, sequences, means and integrals of real or complex numbers: Hardy, Hilbert, Carleman, Wirtinger, Opial, Landau–Kolmogorov, Hermite–Hadamard, Kantorovich and Popoviciu, power-sum and elementary log/exp bounds; inequalities stated with Sobolev norms go to Function spaces, eigenvalue inequalities to Operator theory.

fields.title: Sequences, series and summability
fields.description: Convergence of numerical sequences and series and of series of functions, summability methods and Tauberian theorems, and closed-form evaluation of infinite series and products.

subfields.title: Convergence of sequences and series
subfields.description: Convergence tests (root test, rearrangement theorem, Stolz–Cesàro), normal and uniform convergence of series of functions, and specific limits of sequences and partial sums.

subfields.title: Summability and Tauberian theorems
subfields.description: Matrix summability methods (Silverman–Toeplitz, Cesàro means, permanent methods) and Tauberian theorems of Tauber, Hardy–Littlewood, Wiener and Newman.

subfields.title: Series for π, ζ(3) and other constants
subfields.description: Series and infinite products evaluating constants: π, Catalan's constant, Euler's constant, √2, ζ(3), reciprocal central binomial sums.

subfields.title: Trigonometric and harmonic-number series
subfields.description: Closed forms for series in powers of sin, cos or tan, central binomial series in trigonometric arguments, partial-fraction series of trigonometric functions, and identities with harmonic or odd harmonic numbers, as in Ramanujan's notebooks Chapter 9.

subfields.title: Power series and series transformations
subfields.description: Identities and transformations of power series and exponential-type series: Lagrange inversion and the tree function, Abel- and Jensen-type exponential series, coefficients of exp of a power series and Newton's identities for summable sequences, transformations of factorial series and Taylor-shift transformations, and Touchard / generalized Bell series.

fields.title: Asymptotic analysis
fields.description: Asymptotic expansions and methods: Euler–Maclaurin and Watson's lemma, Laplace-type integrals, coefficient asymptotics of power series (Bender's lemma), Stirling-type and inverse-factorial expansions, and asymptotic expansions of power sums, Lambert series and log sums; complex-analytic saddle-point results on entire functions go to Complex analysis.

fields.title: Special functions
fields.description: Named transcendental functions and their series, integral representations and identities: gamma and digamma, hypergeometric functions, exponential and logarithmic integrals, Lambert W, Bessel, Dickman, Bernoulli polynomials, polylogarithms and Clausen functions, and elliptic functions (elliptic-function topics sit directly in the field).

subfields.title: Gamma and digamma functions
subfields.description: The gamma, digamma and trigamma functions: series and integral representations, factorial series, growth bounds against exponentials, and Ramanujan's digamma identities.

subfields.title: Hypergeometric functions
subfields.description: Generalized and basic hypergeometric series and their summation theorems (Gauss, Dougall, Dixon, Klamkin, Frisch). Orthogonal polynomial families go to Algebra/orthogonal-polynomials.

subfields.title: Exponential, logarithmic and related functions
subfields.description: Exponential, logarithmic and trigonometric-type functions and their relatives: exponential integral E1 and Ein, logarithmic integral, Lambert W, logistic function, x^y = y^x, exponential sums, Mittag-Leffler expansion of 1/(e^u − 1), modified Bessel functions, Dickman–de Bruijn function, Bell-polynomial functions.

subfields.title: Bernoulli polynomials, polylogarithms and Clausen functions
subfields.description: Bernoulli and Euler polynomials and their generating-function identities, Berndt's φ_r and power-difference series, Clausen functions, the inverse tangent integral and dilogarithm identities; results whose content is values of ζ, Dirichlet L or β functions belong to NumberTheory.

fields.title: Complex analysis
fields.description: Holomorphic and meromorphic functions of one and several complex variables: Cauchy theory, entire functions, conformal and univalent maps, zeros of polynomials, and Hilbert and Banach spaces of analytic functions.

subfields.title: Complex integration, residues and singularities
subfields.description: Contour integrals, Cauchy's theorem, residues, argument principle, Rouché, Laurent series, isolated singularities (Casorati–Weierstrass, great Picard), Schwarz reflection, Looman–Menchoff, normal families and local properties of holomorphic functions on discs and annuli.

subfields.title: Entire and meromorphic functions
subfields.description: Growth and value distribution of entire and meromorphic functions: Wiman–Valiron theory and maximum term, Hayman admissibility, Weierstrass factorization, Mittag-Leffler, Liouville-type rigidity, preimages and zeros/ones on lines.

subfields.title: Geometric function theory
subfields.description: Conformal and univalent maps: Riemann mapping, Koebe and Bloch theorems, Schwarz–Pick and half-plane self-maps, starlike and univalent coefficient problems, Loewner equation, holomorphic motions.

subfields.title: Polynomials in the complex plane
subfields.description: Analytic behaviour of complex polynomials: location of zeros (Eneström–Kakeya, Sendov's problem, Jentzsch), flat and Littlewood polynomials, complementary polynomials and sup norms on the unit circle. Algebraic properties of polynomials go to Algebra; Mahler measure goes to NumberTheory.

subfields.title: Several complex variables
subfields.description: Holomorphic functions on C^n: Hartogs extension and separate analyticity, Weierstrass preparation, complex Hessians.

subfields.title: Spaces of analytic functions
subfields.description: Hardy, Bergman, Dirichlet and Fock spaces and their reproducing kernels, H^∞, boundary behaviour (Fatou, F. and M. Riesz), cyclicity and polynomial density.

fields.title: Potential theory
fields.description: Harmonic and subharmonic functions in the plane and in R^n, the maximum principle, harmonic conjugates, the Newton and logarithmic potentials and fundamental solutions of the Laplacian.

fields.title: Harmonic analysis
fields.description: Fourier series, the Fourier transform on R^n, Fourier analysis on finite groups and the Boolean cube, wavelets and multiscale analysis, real-variable methods (maximal functions, the Calderón–Zygmund decomposition, BMO), singular integrals, and other integral transforms and moment problems.

subfields.title: Fourier series
subfields.description: Fourier series on the circle and torus: Fejér and Dirichlet kernels, pointwise and Cesàro convergence, Riemann–Lebesgue, uniqueness, absolutely convergent series and Wiener's theorems, periodic convolution, Fourier optimization on the torus.

subfields.title: Fourier transform and uncertainty principles
subfields.description: The Fourier transform on R^n and Schwartz functions: convolution, Bochner, Hausdorff–Young, Heisenberg and fractal uncertainty, band-limited functions and Bernstein inequalities, sampling and Fourier interpolation, Kakeya sets, Beurling–Ahlfors and other singular integrals.

subfields.title: Discrete Fourier analysis
subfields.description: Fourier analysis on finite abelian groups and the Boolean cube: DFT and FFT, Plancherel, finite uncertainty, Young and Hausdorff–Young, Riesz–Thorin on finite sets, influences and noise operators.

subfields.title: Wavelets and multiscale analysis
subfields.description: Wavelet orthonormal bases and multiresolution approximations, the Haar system, conjugate mirror filters and fast two-channel filter banks, and wavelet scattering transforms built from cascades of wavelet modulus operators. Frames and Riesz bases of general Hilbert spaces are under Hilbert spaces; sparse approximation in bases and dictionaries is under Approximation theory.

subfields.title: Integral transforms and moment problems
subfields.description: Laplace, Mellin and Radon transforms (Ramanujan's master theorem, Fourier slice theorem) and Hausdorff moment problems.

subfields.title: Real-variable methods
subfields.description: Dyadic intervals and stopping times, the dyadic and Hardy–Littlewood maximal functions, the Calderón–Zygmund decomposition, Lebesgue differentiation along dyadic intervals, vector-valued maximal inequalities, bounded mean oscillation, the John–Nirenberg inequality and H¹–BMO duality.

fields.title: Normed groups, rings and fields
fields.description: Norms and seminorms on groups, rings and fields, including ultrametric norms, normed homomorphisms, completions and quotients. Abstract infinite sums belong to Topology, analytic convergence tests to Sequences, series and summability, and equivalence of absolute values and spectral norms on field extensions to p-adic numbers.

fields.title: Banach space theory
fields.description: Normed, Banach and topological vector spaces: duality, weak topologies, geometry of the unit ball, bases and classical sequence spaces.

subfields.title: Normed spaces
subfields.description: Seminormed and normed vector spaces, balls and spheres, finite-dimensional norm equivalence, completions, complemented subspaces, linear isometries, normed affine spaces and operator norms of multilinear and alternating maps. Geometric isometry theorems such as the Mazur–Ulam theorem belong to Geometry of Banach spaces.

subfields.title: Duality, weak topologies and reflexivity
subfields.description: Hahn–Banach, annihilators and bipolars, weak and weak-star convergence and topologies, Goldstine, James, Eberlein–Šmulian, Krein–Šmulian, Banach–Alaoglu, Mazur's lemma, Banach limits, Hamel bases and discontinuous functionals, F-spaces and locally convex spaces, Choquet theory.

subfields.title: Geometry of Banach spaces
subfields.description: Convexity and smoothness of norms (uniform convexity, Kadec–Klee, Birkhoff–James), extreme points of balls, Auerbach and Schauder bases, approximation property, isometries (Banach–Stone, Mazur–Ulam), Banach–Mazur, Dvoretzky–Rogers, Grothendieck, Rademacher type, Daugavet, Bishop–Phelps.

subfields.title: Classical sequence spaces
subfields.description: ℓ^p and c₀: duality, Schauder bases, compactness criteria, Schur and Rosenthal ℓ¹ theorems, Pitt's theorem, quotients of ℓ¹, finite ℓ^p geometry, convolution on ℓ^p(ℤ).

fields.title: Hilbert spaces
fields.description: Geometry of inner product spaces: nearest-point projections, orthonormal and Hilbert bases, separability and ℓ², frames and Riesz bases, weak convergence (Opial, Radon–Riesz), Kirszbraun extension, derivatives of the norm, representer theorems; operators on Hilbert spaces go to Operator theory, analytic RKHS to Complex analysis.

fields.title: Operator theory
fields.description: Bounded linear operators on Banach and Hilbert spaces: spectra, compact and Fredholm operators, shifts and other concrete operators, and eigenvalue inequalities.

subfields.title: Spectral theory
subfields.description: Spectra and spectral theorems: self-adjoint, normal and compact self-adjoint spectral theorems, approximate and essential spectrum, numerical range and radius, Cayley transform, spectra of finite-rank and rank-one operators, almost Mathieu operator.

subfields.title: Compact and Fredholm operators
subfields.description: Compact and finite-rank operators, Schauder's theorem, complete continuity, Hilbert–Schmidt operators, Riesz–Schauder theory, Fredholm alternative and index, closed-range theorems.

subfields.title: Bounded operators and operator topologies
subfields.description: General bounded operators: Douglas lemma, direct sums, strong and weak operator convergence, uniform boundedness, Hellinger–Toeplitz, invariant subspaces (Lomonosov), hypercyclicity criteria, Wold decomposition.

subfields.title: Shift, Toeplitz and Hankel operators
subfields.description: Unilateral, bilateral and weighted shifts and their spectra, indices and numerical ranges, Rolewicz backward shifts, Toeplitz, Hankel and composition operators on ℓ².

subfields.title: Integral, multiplication and diagonal operators
subfields.description: Volterra and kernel integral operators, Cesàro and Hilbert operators, multiplication operators on C(X) and L², diagonal operators, Schur tests, L^p bounds for integral operators.

subfields.title: Eigenvalue inequalities and perturbation
subfields.description: Courant–Fischer, Weyl, Ky Fan, Cauchy interlacing, Schur–Horn, Eckart–Young, Bauer–Fike, Peierls–Klein for self-adjoint operators; statements only about finite matrices move to LinearAlgebra.

fields.title: Banach and operator algebras
fields.description: Banach algebras and C*- and von Neumann algebras: exponentials and product formulas in Banach algebras, GNS, Gelfand–Naimark, bicommutant, Kaplansky density, Russo–Dye, Stinespring, Kadison–Singer and the Marcus–Spielman–Srivastava theorem.

fields.title: Function spaces and Sobolev inequalities
fields.description: L^p and Sobolev spaces of functions: embeddings (Morrey, Rellich, radial, trace), Ehrling, Agmon, Ladyzhenskaya, Gagliardo–Nirenberg and weighted Hardy–Sobolev inequalities, sup-norm bounds by H¹ energy, L^p limits and weak convergence in L^p.

fields.title: Distributions
fields.description: Test functions, Schwartz functions, tempered distributions and distributional derivatives: principal values, Plemelj limits, Dirac comb, partitions of unity.

fields.title: Ordinary differential equations
fields.description: Existence and uniqueness (Cauchy–Peano, Picard, maximal solutions), linear systems and fundamental matrices, stability and Lyapunov's indirect method, Sturm–Liouville and boundary value problems with their Green's operators and eigenfunctions, oscillation and comparison theorems.

fields.title: Control theory
fields.description: Mathematical control theory of finite-dimensional systems: controllability of linear systems (controllability Gramian, Kalman rank condition, Hautus test), pole placement and stabilisation by state feedback, Lie-bracket conditions for nonlinear controllability, Brockett's obstruction to continuous feedback stabilisation and the return method; system identification by recursive least squares and the capability and limits of feedback for uncertain discrete-time systems. Optimal control and dynamic programming are under Convex analysis and calculus of variations and Computer science.

fields.title: Rough paths and path signatures
fields.description: Signatures of paths and controlled differential equations: iterated integrals of a path, Chen's identity, signatures of piecewise-linear paths, the shuffle identity, time reversal and reparametrisation, the Lévy area, signature series of linear controlled equations, uniqueness of the signature up to tree-like equivalence, universal approximation by linear functionals of the signature, and multiplicative functionals of finite p-variation with Lyons's extension theorem. Brownian motion and stochastic integrals are under Probability.

fields.title: Partial differential equations
fields.description: PDE existence, regularity and qualitative results: Cauchy–Kovalevskaya, heat and Airy equations, weak solutions and elliptic regularity, Euler singularity formation, σ₂ Hessian estimates, radial symmetry, viscosity solutions, reaction–diffusion systems and Turing instability, Dirichlet and Neumann spectra of the Laplacian.

fields.title: Convex analysis and calculus of variations
fields.description: Convex functions and sets in analysis and optimization: Fenchel conjugates, polar sets, Moreau decomposition, convex projections, KKT conditions, gradient descent rates, Stampacchia, Tikhonov regularization, Euler–Lagrange, mountain pass and Ekeland principles; linear programming goes to convex geometry. Ridge regression, Tikhonov regularization of a finite-dimensional least-squares problem, is under [least squares, ridge and lasso regression](../../ComputerScience/machine-learning/supervised-learning/least-squares-ridge-and-lasso-regression/README.md) in Machine learning.

fields.title: Fixed-point theory
fields.description: Fixed points of nonexpansive, Lipschitz and affine maps: the Browder–Göhde–Kirk theorem and Kirk's normal structure, Markov–Kakutani, Browder's demiclosedness principle, maps with contracting iterates.

fields.title: Numerical analysis
fields.description: Algorithms with error analysis: bisection and Newton's method, Euler and Runge–Kutta methods, Galerkin and finite element estimates (Céa, Aubin–Nitsche, Strang, Banach–Nečas–Babuška), and methods for smooth unconstrained optimization (line searches and the Zoutendijk condition, nonlinear conjugate gradient, trust-region, quasi-Newton and Barzilai–Borwein methods).

fields.title: Approximation theory
fields.description: Approximation and interpolation of functions: Chebyshev equioscillation, best approximation, the minimax property of Chebyshev polynomials, Chebyshev series and interpolation, Lagrange interpolation, Bernstein polynomials and Voronovskaya, Korovkin, Müntz–Szász, Runge, Kolmogorov superposition, universal approximation, and sparse approximation: best M-term approximation in an orthonormal basis and greedy pursuits (matching pursuit and orthogonal matching pursuit).

Biology.title: Mathematical Biology
Biology.description: Mathematical biology models populations, genomes, and biochemical networks, from coalescents and reaction dynamics to the algorithms that read biological sequences.

fields.title: Population genetics
fields.description: Mathematical models of allele frequencies in populations under random mating, selection, mutation, migration and genetic drift, including the Wright–Fisher and Moran models and their diffusion limits.

subfields.title: Diffusion theory
subfields.description: The Wright–Fisher diffusion as the continuum limit of allele-frequency dynamics: generator and semigroup, fixation probabilities, absorption and sojourn times, mutation and stationary laws, allele age and the Poisson random field.

subfields.title: Selection, migration and transmission
subfields.description: Allele-frequency dynamics under viability selection and biased transmission, migration-selection balance, interference between linked selected loci and modifiers of transmission. Deterministic recurrences and finite-population stochastic interference remain distinct models.

fields.title: Coalescent theory
fields.description: Backward-in-time models of the genealogy of a sample of genes, from Kingman's coalescent and its generalizations to the site frequency spectrum, recombination and population structure.

subfields.title: Cannings models and multiple-merger coalescents
subfields.description: Exchangeable Cannings models of reproduction and the limits of their genealogies: convergence to Kingman's coalescent under the Möhle–Sagitov conditions, Λ-coalescent limits for heavy-tailed offspring, merger rates and the Beta-coalescents, coming down from infinity, and the site frequency spectrum under multiple mergers.

fields.title: Detecting natural selection
fields.description: Statistical tests of neutrality and genome scans for selection based on polymorphism, divergence and haplotype structure, and models of the distribution of fitness effects.

fields.title: Population structure and admixture
fields.description: f-statistics, admixture graphs, ancestry models and linkage-disequilibrium methods for inferring the relationships and mixture histories of populations.

fields.title: Conservation genetics
fields.description: Models coupling the genetics and demography of small or fragmented populations: kinship-minimizing management, genetic diversity summaries, effective-size requirements, genetic rescue and the separate risks of extinction and genetic loss.

fields.title: Phylogenetics
fields.description: Reconstruction of evolutionary trees from sequence data: substitution models, likelihood and parsimony, distance methods, tree metrics, splits and the enumeration of phylogenetic trees.

subfields.title: Phylogenetic inference and comparison
subfields.description: Statistical guarantees and identifiability for evolutionary trees, networks and recorded cell lineages, together with agreement-subtree models for comparing trees. Each article retains its own observation, sampling and evolutionary model.

fields.title: Molecular evolution
fields.description: Models of genome evolution at the molecular level: mutational bias in the introduction of variation, the mutational-hazard view of genome complexity and constructive neutral evolution.

fields.title: Quantitative genetics
fields.description: The genetics of continuously varying traits: decomposition of genetic variance, resemblance between relatives, kinship, mixed models and the response to selection.

fields.title: Statistical genetics
fields.description: Statistical methods for genome-wide association studies, heritability estimation from summary statistics, fine-mapping, Mendelian randomization and gene constraint scores.

subfields.title: Association tests
subfields.description: Tests used in genetic association studies, and their calibration: tests of association between genotypes and a trait (the Cochran–Armitage trend test of genotype counts, the SKAT variance-component test with relatedness, genomic control) and the exact and asymptotic tests of Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium of genotype counts that accompany them. Fisher's exact test, the burden test and SKAT-O, multiple testing across genes, and genomic control with an estimated inflation factor are under Hypothesis testing in Probability.

fields.title: Cancer genomics
fields.description: Mathematical models for tumour sequencing data: purity and copy number, cancer cell fractions, mutation detection power, mutational signatures and the timing of genomic events.

fields.title: Bioinformatics
fields.description: Algorithms and statistical models on biological sequences and data: sequence alignment, genome assembly, motifs, RNA secondary structure, clustering and network reconstruction.

subfields.title: Sequence alignment
subfields.description: Pairwise and multiple alignment of biological sequences: Needleman–Wunsch and Smith–Waterman, affine gaps, banded, linear-space, semi-global and wavefront algorithms.

subfields.title: Statistical models of genomic data
subfields.description: Statistical models, scores and significance tests for functional-genomics measurements: allelic imbalance and allele-specific reporter assays, overdispersed read counts, splicing levels, expression programs and tissue specificity, chromatin accessibility, reproducibility of replicate experiments, protein interaction scoring and the significance of causal-network predictions.

subfields.title: Sequence design and binding prediction
subfields.description: Models that score, predict or select biological sequences for experiments and vaccines: factorizable sequence libraries, likelihoods for measured binding affinities and population coverage of peptide vaccines.

fields.title: Systems biology
fields.description: Dynamics of biochemical reaction networks and gene regulatory circuits: mass-action kinetics, enzyme kinetics, ultrasensitivity, feedback, metabolic flux analysis and gene expression noise.

fields.title: Pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics
fields.description: Compartment models of drug absorption, distribution and elimination, linear and saturable, under bolus, infusion and repeated dosing; dose–response laws, reference models for drug combinations and models of concentration measurements. Enzyme kinetics as such is under Systems biology.

fields.title: Population and evolutionary dynamics
fields.description: Differential-equation and matrix models of population growth, structure, species interaction and evolutionary change, such as logistic growth, predator–prey systems, metapopulations, replicator dynamics, quasispecies and Leslie matrices, and the life tables and direct standardization of demography.

subfields.title: Evolutionary games, graph dynamics and within-host models
subfields.description: Stochastic and game-theoretic models of evolution and of populations inside hosts: Moran processes and games on graphs, with amplifiers of selection and fixation probabilities and times; repeated games and the evolution of cooperation; and models of viruses and tumours within a host, of competing microbes and of replicators in protocells.

fields.title: Reaction–diffusion and pattern formation
fields.description: Reaction–diffusion models of biological spread and spatial patterning, including travelling waves, morphogen gradients and Turing instabilities.

fields.title: Mathematical neuroscience
fields.description: Models of excitable membranes and neurons: the Nernst potential and passive cable theory, the Hodgkin–Huxley and FitzHugh–Nagumo equations, integrate-and-fire neurons and Wilson–Cowan models of neural populations.

fields.title: Mathematical epidemiology
fields.description: Compartmental, renewal and branching-process models of infectious disease transmission and their reproduction numbers, the reporting of incidence, and the accuracy of diagnostic tests.

subfields.title: Parasite relatedness and genomic epidemiology
subfields.description: Identity by descent between malaria parasites: expected relatedness of parasite genealogies, classification of genealogical relationships, relatedness of cotransmitted parasites and the heterozygosity of polygenomic infections.

subfields.title: Treatment, drug resistance and immune escape
subfields.description: Transmission and within-host models under treatment and vaccination: competition between drug-sensitive and resistant strains, escape from regional vaccination, and viral dynamics under antiviral therapy.

subfields.title: Chronic disease and social contagion
subfields.description: Models of non-communicable health states: multistate and lifetime risks of chronic disease, latent signatures of multimorbidity, and contagion with spontaneous adoption of behaviours and health states.

CategoryTheory.title: Category Theory
CategoryTheory.description: Category theory organizes mathematical structures through morphisms, functors, universal properties, limits, and adjunctions.

fields.title: Categories, functors and natural transformations
fields.description: The basic language of category theory: categories, functors, natural transformations and isomorphisms, monomorphisms and epimorphisms, equivalences, full and faithful functors, opposite and functor categories, the Yoneda lemma and representable functors, skeleta and size conditions.

fields.title: Constructions of categories
fields.description: Categories built from other categories: products, sums and joins, comma, arrow, slice and structured-arrow categories, categories of elements and the Grothendieck construction, full and wide subcategories, quotient and path categories, idempotent completion, graded objects and diagrams of composable arrows.

fields.title: Special categories and examples
fields.description: Particular categories and kinds of categories: the categories of types, of categories and of quivers, groupoids, preorders, discrete, thin, finite and single-object categories, concrete categories with their forgetful functors, and categories of objects with a monoid action. Categories of algebraic or topological objects are with the corresponding algebra and topology fields.

fields.title: Classes of morphisms and objects
fields.description: Properties of morphisms and of objects and their stability under composition, base change and limits: special epimorphisms, subobjects and subfunctors, generators and separators, lifting properties, weak factorization systems and the small object argument, and closure of classes of objects under limits, colimits and extensions.

fields.title: Limits and colimits
fields.description: Universal cones and cocones over diagrams: their existence, preservation, reflection and creation by functors, particular shapes such as products, pullbacks, equalizers, kernels and ends, filtered colimits and final functors, and ind-objects.

subfields.title: Limits of diagrams
subfields.description: Universal properties, existence results and constructions of limits and colimits, including pointwise limits of functors, limits in slice categories and iterated limits.

subfields.title: Shapes of limits and colimits
subfields.description: Initial and terminal objects, products, pullbacks, equalizers, kernels, images, ends and their duals. Biproducts are with additive categories.

subfields.title: Filtered diagrams and ind-objects
subfields.description: Filtered and cofiltered diagrams, sifted categories, final functors, transfinite diagrams and ind-completions. Cardinal bounds on filteredness are treated in accessible categories.

subfields.title: Preservation and creation of limits
subfields.description: Continuity and exactness properties of functors, including preservation, reflection and creation of limits and colimits of particular shapes.

fields.title: Adjunctions and Kan extensions
fields.description: Adjoint functors, units and counits, mates, reflective subcategories and adjoint functor theorems, adjoint triples, Kan extensions along functors, dense functors, exact squares and profunctors; monads are in their own field.

fields.title: Monads and algebras
fields.description: Monads and comonads, their Eilenberg–Moore and Kleisli categories, monadicity and comonadicity theorems, and algebras and coalgebras of endofunctors.

fields.title: Localization of categories
fields.description: Formally inverting a class of morphisms: localization functors and their universal property, the calculus of fractions, morphisms of localizers, Bousfield localization, and the localization of functors in several variables and of additive and monoidal structures; derived categories are in homological algebra.

fields.title: Accessible and locally presentable categories
fields.description: Categories generated under highly filtered colimits by a set of small objects: κ-filtered categories, presentable objects and accessible functors, locally presentable and accessible categories, and the orthogonal-reflection construction.

fields.title: Regular, extensive and adhesive categories
fields.description: Exactness properties of categories with finite limits and colimits: effective epimorphisms and regular categories, internal equivalence relations, extensive and distributive categories, universal and van Kampen colimits, and adhesive categories; abelian categories are in their own field.

fields.title: Monoidal categories
fields.description: Monoidal categories equip a category with a tensor product and unit object, with braided and symmetric variants governing how tensor factors may be exchanged.

fields.title: Enriched categories
fields.description: Categories whose hom-objects lie in a monoidal category: enriched categories and functors, enriched functor categories, ordinary categories with an enrichment, conical limits and the bicategory of enriched categories.

fields.title: Bicategories and higher categories
fields.description: Bicategories and 2-categories: lax, oplax and pseudofunctors, their transformations and modifications, coherence, adjunctions, mates and Kan extensions inside a bicategory, spans and the bicategorical Yoneda embedding. Quasi-categories and other simplicial models are in algebraic topology.

fields.title: Fibered categories and descent
fields.description: Functors viewed as families of categories: cartesian and cocartesian morphisms, fibered and cofibered categories, the Grothendieck construction for pseudofunctors, descent data, prestacks and stacks, and descent of properties of morphisms.

fields.title: Sites and sheaves
fields.description: Grothendieck topologies, sieves, coverages and pretopologies, sheaves on sites with values in a category, sheafification, continuous and cocontinuous functors, dense subsites, the coherent and canonical topologies, hypercovers, points of sites and sheaf cohomology.

fields.title: Topos theory
fields.description: Topos theory studies elementary and Grothendieck toposes, categories with finite limits, exponentials and a subobject classifier that behave like universes of sets.

fields.title: Galois categories
fields.description: Grothendieck's axiomatic Galois theory: Galois categories and fiber functors, Galois objects, pro-representability of fiber functors, and the fundamental group of a Galois category with its action on fibers.

fields.title: Additive and abelian categories
fields.description: Categories enriched in abelian groups and modules: preadditive, additive and linear categories, biproducts and additive functors, abelian categories and their embedding theorems, Grothendieck abelian categories and the AB axioms, and Serre classes; complexes, resolutions and derived functors are in homological algebra.

fields.title: Triangulated categories
fields.description: Categories with a shift functor and distinguished triangles: shifts and functors commuting with them, pretriangulated and triangulated categories, triangulated functors and subcategories, Verdier localization, homological functors and t-structures with their hearts; derived categories of abelian categories are in homological algebra.

fields.title: Homological algebra
fields.description: Homological algebra studies abelian categories through projective resolutions and the derived functors they define, such as Tor, together with their additivity.

subfields.title: Complexes and homology
subfields.description: Chain and cochain complexes indexed by complex shapes, short complexes, homology and exactness, diagram lemmas such as the snake and five lemmas, long exact homology sequences, quasi-isomorphisms, bicomplexes, total complexes and truncations; abelian categories as such are in the additive and abelian categories field.

subfields.title: Homotopy and derived categories
subfields.description: Chain homotopies, mapping cones and cylinders, the homotopy category of complexes and its triangulated structure, derived categories obtained by inverting quasi-isomorphisms, and dg modules and dg categories with their coherent nerves and derived Morita theory; triangulated categories in general are in the triangulated categories field.

subfields.title: Resolutions and derived functors
subfields.description: Projective and injective objects, resolutions and dimensions, left and right derived functors of additive functors, Ext and Tor, and derived functors between localized categories via derivability structures.

subfields.title: Spectral sequences
subfields.description: Spectral objects and spectral sequences, their pages and convergence, and the spectral sequences of filtered and double complexes.

fields.title: Condensed mathematics
fields.description: Sheaves on profinite sets and compact Hausdorff spaces for the coherent topology: condensed and light condensed sets and modules, discrete condensed objects, solid modules, and the comparison with topological spaces.

Combinatorics.title: Combinatorics
Combinatorics.description: Combinatorics studies finite and discrete configurations through counting, extremal structure, and constructive arguments.

fields.title: Binomial coefficients and identities
fields.description: Binomial, multinomial and generalized binomial coefficients and closed-form evaluation of finite sums built from them (alternating, reciprocal, harmonic-weighted, hypergeometric), including Apéry-like sequences such as Franel, Domb and Zagier numbers; q-binomials go to symmetric functions and q-analogues, Catalan-type numbers to Catalan numbers, Stirling-weighted sums to Stirling numbers.

subfields.title: Binomial sums and hypergeometric identities
subfields.description: Evaluations and bounds of sums of products of binomial coefficients: Chu–Vandermonde, Dixon, Knuth's old sum, Staver, Frisch, Klamkin, hockey-stick and Filipponi identities, partial-sum bounds, multisection identities, and Franel, Domb, Zagier and Catalan–Larcombe–French numbers defined by binomial sums.

subfields.title: Central binomial coefficients and harmonic sums
subfields.description: Finite sums and power series involving central binomial coefficients or their reciprocals, often weighted by harmonic or odd harmonic numbers, including arcsin-type series and Kollár's incomplete binomial sums.

subfields.title: Generalized binomial coefficients and Pascal-like triangles
subfields.description: Variants of the binomial coefficient and of Pascal's triangle: b-ary and digital (carry-free) binomial coefficients, Ward and totienomial coefficients from generalized factorials, trinomial and quadrinomial coefficients, rascal, hyperbolic Pascal and 2-Pascal triangles and their diagonals; the Pascal matrix viewed as a Riordan array goes to Riordan arrays.

fields.title: Catalan numbers and lattice paths
fields.description: The Catalan family of counting sequences and the lattice paths they count: Catalan, Fuss–Catalan, Narayana, Motzkin, Schröder, Fine and Riordan numbers, Dyck and Motzkin paths and their statistics, Delannoy numbers and walks with prescribed steps, including arithmetic properties (parity, integrality, perfect powers) of these numbers.

subfields.title: Catalan numbers and their generalizations
subfields.description: Catalan numbers and generalizations defined by formulas or recurrences: Fuss–Catalan, super Catalan, (p,q)-Patalan, Whitt and Sabar arrays, generalized Catalan–Schröder, Fine and Riordan numbers, Narayana numbers and polynomials, Touchard's identity, Raney's cycle lemma, and divisibility or growth of these numbers.

subfields.title: Motzkin numbers and Motzkin paths
subfields.description: Motzkin numbers and paths: colored, weighted and (u,l,d) Motzkin paths, humps and peaks, the Motzkin triangle, links with central trinomial coefficients, alternating Motzkin sums, Aigner's inequality, and Motzkin-related sequences such as A005773; weighted Motzkin paths used to compute Hankel determinants go to Hankel determinants and continued fractions.

subfields.title: Dyck paths and lattice walks
subfields.description: Statistics on Dyck paths (peaks, valleys, marked steps, subwords) and their variants (skew, rational, k-box Dyck paths), lattice walks with unit or diagonal steps, Delannoy numbers, Sulanke arrays, colored Dyck paths, and nonintersecting paths via the Lindström–Gessel–Viennot lemma.

fields.title: Stirling, Bell and Eulerian numbers
fields.description: The number triangles and sequences that count set partitions, permutations by cycles, descents and excedances, and their relatives: Stirling and Lah numbers and their generalizations, Bell and Fubini numbers and Bell polynomials, Eulerian numbers and polynomials, and Bernoulli, Euler and Genocchi numbers studied combinatorially.

subfields.title: Stirling and Lah numbers
subfields.description: Classical Stirling numbers of the first and second kind and Lah numbers: recurrences, explicit and addition formulas, rising and falling factorial expansions, orthogonality and inverse Stirling matrices, cycle counts, inequalities and identities such as Lee's and Gy's.

subfields.title: Generalized Stirling numbers
subfields.description: Deformations and generalizations of Stirling numbers: r-Stirling, associated Stirling, Hsu–Shiue, Jacobi–Stirling, Legendre–Stirling, meromorphic and degenerate Stirling numbers, α-Stirling and generalized Stirling matrices, and (q,r)-Whitney and Dowling numbers.

subfields.title: Bell numbers, Fubini numbers and Bell polynomials
subfields.description: Bell numbers (Dobinski, Spivey, Touchard and Turán-type identities, log-convexity), complete, partial and generalized Bell polynomials, potential polynomials, Fubini (ordered Bell) numbers and their congruences, and horse numbers.

subfields.title: Eulerian numbers and polynomials
subfields.description: Counting permutations by descents or excedances: Eulerian numbers and polynomials, refined, multiset and generalized Eulerian polynomials, associated Stirling–Eulerian numbers, Worpitzky's identity, gamma-positivity and Hankel determinants of Eulerian polynomials, Bell permutations by weak excedances.

subfields.title: Bernoulli, Euler and Genocchi numbers
subfields.description: Combinatorial formulas for Bernoulli, Euler, tangent and Genocchi numbers (Garabedian's formulas, median Euler and Genocchi numbers, Euler–Seidel matrices, Carlitz q-Bernoulli polynomials), their divisibility, and sums of powers via Faulhaber coefficients.

fields.title: Riordan arrays and sequence transforms
fields.description: Infinite lower-triangular arrays and operators on sequences studied through generating functions: the Riordan group, number triangles and their diagonals, binomial, INVERT and Catalan transforms, Hankel and Toeplitz determinants and continued fractions; a specific named family (Motzkin triangle, Stirling matrices) stays with that family.

subfields.title: Riordan arrays and number triangles
